llm.answer:
**Core Graphics – Apple Developer Documentation (PDF)** *(All information is drawn from the three pages of the same PDF that you uploaded.)* | Category | Key Points | Source | |----------|------------|--------| | **Framework Overview** | • Core Graphics is built on Apple’s Quartz 2‑D drawing engine.
• It delivers lightweight, low‑level 2‑D rendering with high‑fidelity output.
• Core Graphics handles path‑based drawing, geometric transformations, color management, off‑screen rendering, patterns, gradients, shading, image data management, image creation, image masking, and PDF document creation, display, and parsing.
• On macOS it also includes services for working with display hardware, low‑level user‑input events, and the windowing system. | [Source 1] | | **Geometric Data Types** | • **CGFloat** – basic floating‑point scalar type.
• **CGPoint** – point with x/y coordinates.
• **CGSize** – width/height dimensions.
• **CGRect** – rectangle defined by origin and size.
• **CGVector** – two‑dimensional vector.
• **CGAffineTransform** – 2‑D linear transformation matrix. | [Source 2] | | **Core Classes & Structures** | • **CGContext** – the Quartz 2‑D drawing environment.
• **CGImage** – bitmap image or image mask.
• **CGPath / CGMutablePath** – immutable/ mutable geometric paths.
• **CGLayer** – off‑screen context for reusable content.
• **CGColor / CGColorSpace** – color components and color‑space definitions.
• **CGFont** – glyph and layout information for text.
• **CGPDFDocument** – container for PDF drawing information.
• **CGDataConsumer / CGDataProvider** – abstractions for raw data write/read.
• **CGShading / CGGradient** – smooth color transitions for radial/axial fills.
• **CGFunction** – callback‑based function for shading.
• **CGPattern** – 2‑D pattern for drawing paths. | [Source 2] | | **Quartz Services** | • **QuartzDisplayServices** – direct access to macOS Window Server for configuring display hardware.
• **QuartzEventServices** – manage event taps (filters) for observing/altering low‑level user‑input streams.
• **QuartzWindowServices** – provide information about windows managed by the macOS Window Server. | [Source 3] | | **Enumerations, Constants & Functions** | • The PDF lists a comprehensive set of enumerations (e.g., `CGImageComponent`, `CGBitmapLayout`), constants, and low‑level functions that support the framework’s operations. | [Source 3] | | **Platform & Language Support** | • Available on iOS 2.0+, iPadOS 2.0+, macOS 10.8+, tvOS 9.0+, visionOS 1.0+, watchOS 2.0+.
• APIs are documented for Swift (and Objective‑C). | [Source 1] | ### Take‑away Summary Core Graphics is the foundational 2‑D graphics engine on Apple platforms, exposing a rich set of low‑level types, classes, and services that let developers: 1. **Draw and transform** shapes, paths, and text with high precision. 2. **Manage color** through color spaces, shading, gradients, and patterns. 3. **Handle images** (creation, masking, off‑screen rendering). 4. **Create, display, and parse PDFs**. 5. **Interact with the system** (display hardware, user input, windowing) via Quartz services. All of these capabilities are exposed through a consistent API surface that is available across iOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS.
